answers.label: Q.1
answers.finalAnswer: people are demanding changes and pointing to new goals for society; food self-sufficiency, science and technology, industrialisation; no longer willing to be taken for granted or taken for a ride; empathy for all, solving economic disparity and injustice, wider mass consciousness, a true sense of history, participatory decision-making; the old prejudices of the past and structures of exploitation and tyranny; deep shock or distress; to pull down or destroy; cruel and unjust use of power
answers.solution:
(a) The positive aspect of the present turmoil is that the people of India are demanding changes and are pointing towards the new goals that society should set for itself. Problems such as damage to the environment and new sources of energy are also being debated with great passion.

(b) The nation has achieved self-sufficiency in food and made progress in science and technology and in industrialisation.

(c) The author praises the common Indian citizen because he is no longer willing to be taken for granted or taken for a ride.

(d) For society to grow, it must view the problems of all its people with empathy, find solutions to economic disparities and injustice, enlarge mass consciousness, promote a true sense of history instead of blind belief in myths, and start processes of participatory decision-making.

(e) The old, harmful prejudices of the past (printed as 'part', a misprint for 'past') must be eradicated, and the structures of exploitation and tyranny must be demolished.

(f) (i) Trauma: a deeply painful or shocking experience; great distress.
(ii) Demolish: to pull down or destroy completely.
(iii) Tyranny: cruel and unjust use of power over others.

answers.label: Q.2
answers.finalAnswer: Precis titled 'Little Things Reveal Character': character is built by small daily acts; courteous behaviour pleases others and ourselves; anyone can learn gentleness, which is stronger than force.
answers.solution:
Title: Little Things Reveal Character

Small things reveal a person's character, just as light shows through tiny holes. Character is built from small daily acts done well and honestly. The best test of character is how we behave towards others. Polite behaviour to superiors, juniors and equals pleases them because it shows respect, but it pleases us even more. Anyone, rich or poor, can teach himself to be kind and courteous. Gentleness quietly influences everyone, like light, and achieves far more than force.

(78 words)

answers.label: Q.3
answers.finalAnswer: with two thousand sheep (and the sheep-men); they would not eat or drink and kept bleating; five hundred sheep had died; it pushed its pleading face through the bars, waiting to be stroked and loved like a lost pet; it had no fear of man or sea and was tame like a child's pet; pens; sheep-men
answers.solution:
(a) The poet started from Baltimore with twice a thousand, that is two thousand, sheep on board the ship, along with the sheep-men who looked after them.

(b) In the beginning the sheep were miserable. They would not eat and would not drink, and they kept bleating over the sea.

(c) By the time they reached the mouth of the river Mersey, five hundred of the sheep had died.

(d) The poem as printed does not use the word 'waiting'. The sheep stuck its pleading face through the bars of the pen, as if waiting to be stroked and loved. It was tame, and the poet felt it was some child's lost pet who missed the love it was used to.

(e) This sheep was special because it had no fear of man or sea. Unlike the others, it was tame: it pushed its pleading face through the bars and let the poet stroke it. It seemed to be a child's pet, and even the rough, ragged sheep-men stroked its black nose every time they passed it.

(f) (i) A place where sheep are kept: pens
(ii) Shepherds: sheep-men

answers.label: Q.4
answers.finalAnswer: Two paragraphs of about 100 words: (b) television as an idiot box; (c) a bird in hand is worth two in the bush.
answers.solution:
Paragraphs written on (b) and (c).

(b) Television Is Rightly Called an Idiot Box

Television was invented to inform, educate and entertain us. Today, however, it is often called an idiot box, and rightly so. Many people, especially children, sit before it for hours watching cartoons, serials and advertisements without thinking. Their eyesight suffers, they become lazy and they find no time for books, games or family talk. Some programmes are full of violence and silly quarrels, which spoil young minds. Yet the fault lies not in the set but in the viewer. If we choose good programmes like news, quizzes and science shows and watch them for a limited time, television can be a window to the world.

(c) A Bird in Hand Is Worth Two in the Bush

This proverb means that what we already have is worth more than something bigger that we only hope to get. A bird held in the hand is sure, while two birds in a bush may fly away at any moment. Greedy people often lose what they have while running after more. In the old fable, a dog dropped his bone into the stream when he tried to snatch the bone from his own reflection. In the same way, a man who leaves a steady job for a doubtful dream may end up with nothing. We should be ambitious, but we must not give up a sure gain for an uncertain one.

answers.label: Q.5
answers.finalAnswer: Description of the cartoon: leaders pose under a 'Cleanliness Drive' banner amid garbage while three monkeys say 'See no dirt, Smell no dirt, Touch no dirt'; cleanliness needs action, not slogans.
answers.solution:
A Cleanliness Drive Only in Name

The picture shows a building with a large banner reading 'Cleanliness Drive'. Two men, one of them a leader in a white kurta and dhoti, stand under it smiling proudly, as if posing for the cameras. Yet all around their feet lie heaps of garbage, waste paper and rubbish. They do not seem to notice it at all.

On the right sit three monkeys, just like Gandhiji's famous three monkeys. Below them are boards that say 'See no dirt', 'Smell no dirt' and 'Touch no dirt'. Gandhiji's monkeys taught us to keep away from evil, but these monkeys show how people shut their eyes and noses to the filth around them and refuse to touch it.

The cartoon makes fun of those who treat cleanliness as a slogan or a photo opportunity. Banners, speeches and photographs cannot clean a town. Real cleanliness begins when each one of us picks up a broom, puts waste in the dustbin and keeps our surroundings clean every day. Only then will a cleanliness drive be more than a show.

answers.label: Q.6
answers.finalAnswer: Letter to the Editor, The Hindu, by Manoj Pandey of Dehradun on how co-curricular activities build the all-round development of students.
answers.solution:
15, Rajpur Road
Dehradun
Uttarakhand

10 December 2018

The Editor
The Hindu
New Delhi

Subject: Importance of co-curricular activities for students

Sir,

Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to express my views on the importance of co-curricular activities in the all-round development of students.

Today many schools and parents care only about marks. Students spend the whole day with books and coaching classes, and have no time for games, music, debates or drama. This is a serious mistake. Education should develop the body, the mind and the character, not the memory alone.

Sports keep students fit and teach them team spirit and discipline. Debates and quizzes build confidence and the ability to speak in public. Music, art and dance bring out their creativity, while NCC, scouting and social service teach leadership and a sense of duty to the nation. Such activities also relieve the stress of studies.

I request schools to give these activities a regular place in the timetable, and parents to encourage their children to take part in them.

Yours faithfully
Manoj Pandey

answers.label: Q.7
answers.finalAnswer: Morning-assembly speech: man kills for greed and power, destroys nature and builds deadly weapons, so he is the most dangerous animal, but he can choose peace.
answers.solution:
Man Is the Most Dangerous Animal in the World

Good morning to our respected Principal, teachers and dear friends. Today I shall speak on the topic 'Man is the most dangerous animal in the world'.

We fear the tiger, the snake and the shark, but these animals kill only for food or to protect themselves. Man kills for greed, power and pleasure. He has cut down forests, polluted the air and rivers, and wiped out many kinds of animals. He has made guns, bombs and nuclear weapons that can destroy the whole earth. Wars, terrorism and crime are all his work. No animal has harmed its own home and its own kind as much as man has.

Yet man is also the only animal blessed with reason and a conscience. If he uses his mind for peace and kindness, he can protect the world instead of destroying it. Let us choose that path.

Thank you.

answers.label: Q.8
answers.finalAnswer: The chair is made of wood.; The number of board members is very small.; She is the cleverest girl in the class.; We don't agree with what Mr Sharma says.; He wishes the train moved faster.
answers.solution:
(a) The chair is made of wood.
('Wood' as a material is uncountable and takes no article.)

(b) The number of board members is very small.
('The number of' is singular.)

(c) She is the cleverest girl in the class.
(Do not use 'most' with 'cleverest'; use 'in' with a place or group.)

(d) We don't agree with what Mr Sharma says.
(We agree with a person or an opinion, and agree to a proposal.)

(e) He wishes the train moved faster.
(After 'wish' for an unreal present, the verb goes into the past.)

answers.label: Q.10
answers.finalAnswer: their servant had run away; if anything was missing; her gold watch was missing; she had kept it; was going to the police station to report it
answers.solution:
(a) their servant had run away.
(b) if anything was missing.
(c) her gold watch was missing.
(d) she had kept it. (She replied that she had kept it on the dressing table, as usual.)
(e) was going to the police station to report it.

In indirect speech the tenses move one step back (has run becomes had run, is becomes was, did keep becomes had kept, am going becomes was going), and 'our' and 'my' change to suit the speaker.

answers.label: Q.11
answers.finalAnswer: No sooner does the newspaper reach the stands than it is sold out.; My father never fails to go for a walk every morning.; His injured foot prevented him from completing the race.; In all probability, John has forgotten the date of examination.; Only if you come will I go out.
answers.solution:
(a) No sooner does the newspaper reach the stands than it is sold out.
('No sooner' is followed by the helping verb before the subject, and by 'than'.)

(b) My father never fails to go for a walk every morning.

(c) His injured foot prevented him from completing the race.

(d) In all probability, John has forgotten the date of examination.

(e) Only if you come will I go out.
(After 'Only if ...', the main clause takes the helping verb before the subject.)

(b) (i) knowing latest things. 'In the swim' means up to date and involved in what is happening.

answers.finalAnswer: Let the recently painted windows which are far from the main door be opened.; Why is a song being sung by you when everyone is in the land of nod?; The candy which was bought by you yesterday does not taste sweet.; Was it not known to them that you are the son of a cricketer?; A car could be bought by him if he wanted.
answers.solution:
(a) Let the recently painted windows which are far from the main door be opened.
(An order becomes 'Let ... be + past participle'.)

(b) Why is a song being sung by you when everyone is in the land of nod?

(c) The candy which was bought by you yesterday does not taste sweet.
(Only the clause 'you bought yesterday' has an object, so only that part changes.)

(d) Was it not known to them that you are the son of a cricketer?
